submission.bindingBasis: planningEvidence plannedCheckpoint frontier=beta-complete; task.checkpoint requires expectedRevision; consequenceBoundaryEvidence shows Task revision advanced after planning, so the plan's expectedRevision is stale and must be re-presented against the current revision.
submission.rationale: The owner contract states task.checkpoint requires expectedRevision, and stale expectedRevision fails with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed. The boundary evidence confirms the Task revision advanced after planning, so the originally planned checkpoint action (frontier=beta-complete) is now using a stale revision. However, the contract also states "after resume a semantically still-applicable checkpoint may be rebased onto the current revision." But since I have not re-observed the current Task state, I cannot confirm the semantic applicability on the new revision. REBASE_AND_ACT would require knowing the current revision to rebase onto. Given uncertainty about the exact current revision contents, REPLAY_EXACT re-presents the intended consequence (checkpoint beta as complete) against the owner at the boundary, letting the owner determine whether it still applies to the current revision — this avoids falsely claiming a new consequence while preserving the intended action. This maximizes lexicographic optimization: no false/duplicate consequence (not rebasing to a new revision blindly), preserves progress by presenting the checkpoint, and minimizes extra coordination.
